correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts the support geometry for two-point sets. If the unoriented differences differ, all four translations are distinct and each row is a point-mass Fourier transform. If they agree, the three rows have spatial support sizes \(1,2,1\); the middle two-point Fourier polynomial has a zero exactly when the coefficient ratio lies in the group of \(p\)-th roots, and then the zero is unique. This proves all quantifiers for every prime \(p\ge5\).

value.rationale: The two-sparse stratum is the first nontrivial sparse setting for finite STFT support. The theorem completely resolves its support spectrum for all prime cyclic groups and separates the additive-geometric alignment condition from the coefficient-phase cancellation condition. This is a natural exact boundary case for sparse time-frequency uncertainty.
